Bottom-up: 3/Y implied ~$40.5k each -> ~$19.4B + other models ~$0.7B, minus 1-2% discounting -> auto sales ~$19.8B; credits+leasing ~$0.5B; energy ~$3.2B; services ~$4.7B -> ~$28.3B. calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: Q3 deliveries 486,532, storage 13.7 GWh, Q2 revenue $28.236B, consensus $27.6-27.9B. The apparent conflict over revenue per vehicle ($41.7k vs $42.7k) was settled arithmetically: one figure is car sales only, the other the full automotive segment including $146M credits and $364M leasing. Whether the consensus incorporates the delivery beat cannot be verified without web access; I treat it as partly stale. My own mix-adjusted build (3/Y at ~$40.5k, other models ~$85k) gives ~$28.3B after a 1-2% discount haircut. That lands near the runs because the evidence does, not by averaging. Escape probability past either bound judged negligible, so not declared.
